attachments.origin_landmark: transverse processes C7-T6 and articular processes C4-C6
attachments.insertion_landmark: between the superior and inferior nuchal lines, medially

functional_compartments.name: Single fiber population
functional_compartments.function_note: The bulkiest muscle of the posterior neck and the main extensor of the head. The greater occipital nerve pierces it before piercing trapezius, which is one of the described entrapment points in occipital neuralgia.
functional_compartments.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

ultrasound_injection_approach.transducer_placement: High-frequency linear probe placed longitudinally over the posterior neck between the external occipital protuberance and mastoid process, then swept toward the C2 spinous process to visualize the muscle deep to trapezius (and splenius capitis more laterally).
ultrasound_injection_approach.depth_layer: Deep to trapezius, superficial to obliquus capitis inferior -- one of the deep suboccipital extensor layer muscles.
ultrasound_injection_approach.identification_cues: The greater occipital nerve pierces the muscle at approximately 13 mm lateral to the midline and 28 mm inferior to the external occipital protuberance, about 2 cm deep to skin; the third occipital nerve pierces it about 12 mm lateral and 61 mm inferior to the same landmark. Both nerve piercing-points are useful position/depth checkpoints on ultrasound.
structures_at_risk: greater occipital nerve (pierces the muscle roughly 2.8 cm below the external occipital protuberance)
third occipital nerve (pierces the muscle roughly 6.1 cm below the external occipital protuberance)
ultrasound_injection_approach.notes: Semispinalis capitis was one of nine cervical muscle pairs in a cadaveric comparison of ultrasound-guided vs non-guided (palpation-based) injection; pooled across all nine muscles, ultrasound guidance was substantially more accurate (88.2% vs 48.0%), though a per-muscle accuracy figure for semispinalis capitis specifically was not given in the available text.
ultrasound_injection_approach.source: Kim HS, Shin KJ, O J, Kwon HJ, Lee M, Yang HM, 'Stereotactic topography of the greater and third occipital nerves and its clinical implication', Sci Rep 8(1):870 (2018), doi:10.1038/s41598-018-19249-6 -- 30 cadavers (60 sides), 3D-digitizer mapping of nerve piercing points relative to the external occipital protuberance. Retrieved via PubMed. Injection-accuracy context from Kreisler A, Gerrebout C, Defebvre L, Demondion X, 'Accuracy of non-guided versus ultrasound-guided injections in cervical muscles: a cadaver study', J Neurol 268(5):1894-1902 (2021), doi:10.1007/s00415-020-10365-w. Retrieved via PubMed.

trigger_points.location_description: Posterior cervical TrP2, mid-belly 2-4 cm below the occiput.
trigger_points.referred_pain_pattern: A band of pain from the occiput over the side of the head to the temple and forehead ('headache band above the ear').
trigger_points.source: Simons, Travell & Simons Trigger Point Manual -- as cited in this atlas's uploaded head and neck muscle reference document (Simons DG, Travell JG, Simons LS, Myofascial Pain and Dysfunction: The Trigger Point Manual, Vol 1, 2nd ed., Williams & Wilkins, 1999; Donnelly JM, Fernandez-de-las-Penas C, Finnegan M, Freeman JL (eds), 3rd ed., Wolters Kluwer, 2019)

trigger_points.location_description: Posterior cervical TrP3, just below the occipital ridge, near the greater occipital nerve.
trigger_points.referred_pain_pattern: Occipital pain; entrapment of the greater occipital nerve here can cause numbness, tingling and burning over the occipital scalp.
trigger_points.source: Simons, Travell & Simons Trigger Point Manual -- as cited in this atlas's uploaded head and neck muscle reference document (Simons DG, Travell JG, Simons LS, Myofascial Pain and Dysfunction: The Trigger Point Manual, Vol 1, 2nd ed., Williams & Wilkins, 1999; Donnelly JM, Fernandez-de-las-Penas C, Finnegan M, Freeman JL (eds), 3rd ed., Wolters Kluwer, 2019)
